# onpager_schedule_override (Resource)

Manage one override declaration for a schedule, independently of parent settings and sibling declarations.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Local timestamps use the provider request timezone. Explicit Z/offset
# values can also be supplied and always identify absolute instants.
resource "onpager_schedule_override" "example" {
  schedule_id = var.schedule_id
  user_id     = var.user_id
  starts_at   = "2027-01-05T09:00:00"
  ends_at     = "2027-01-05T17:00:00"
}

variable "schedule_id" {
  description = "Existing enabled schedule UUID owned by an active team."
  type        = string
}

variable "user_id" {
  description = "Existing active member UUID of the schedule's team."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ends_at` (String) Exclusive whole-second end in local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or explicit-offset RFC3339 form; zero-only fractional digits are accepted. Source and UTC years must be 0001 through 9999. Must follow `starts_at`. Primary rotations may omit this or use `null` for no end; overrides require a finite end. An empty string is invalid. Equivalent timestamp spellings retain the configured value across request-timezone response changes. Local input is sent unchanged and resolved by the backend in the provider request timezone; DST ambiguity or gaps return API diagnostics. Explicit offsets always identify absolute instants. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local input.
- `schedule_id` (String) Owning schedule UUID. Changing it replaces this child declaration; parent settings and sibling rotations remain independent. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `starts_at` (String) Recurrence anchor for a primary rotation, or inclusive start for an override. Use a whole-second local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or explicit-offset RFC3339 timestamp; zero-only fractional digits are accepted. Source and UTC years must be 0001 through 9999. Equivalent timestamp spellings retain the configured value across request-timezone response changes. Local input is sent unchanged and resolved by the backend in the provider request timezone; DST ambiguity or gaps return API diagnostics. Explicit offsets always identify absolute instants. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local input. Must precede `ends_at` when set.
- `user_id` (String) User UUID assigned for this one-off interval. The user must be an active member of the owning team; no membership is created implicitly. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `request_timezone` (String) Explicit provider request timezone last applied to local datetime inputs. Null when the provider timezone is omitted or all inputs have explicit offsets. Changing the explicit provider timezone plans an update for local inputs; refresh alone preserves saved instants. The backend interprets local clocks and reports DST ambiguity or nonexistent times.
- `revision` (Number) This child rotation's revision, used in strong numeric `If-Match` for declaration replacement and retirement. Independent of parent settings, siblings, and aggregate revision. Stale writes report a conflict.

## Import

Import using `schedule_uuid/override_uuid`. Import reads the stable one-off
declaration, independently of the current occurrence.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_schedule_override.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_schedule_override.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns one one-off schedule override. The user must be an active
member of the owning team. Reference the membership's `user_id` so Terraform
creates the membership first and retires the override before revoking it.

Updates replace the entire planned interval and user, including past planned
coverage, while retaining immutable rule versions and captured notification
facts. Locks, authority and participant eligibility can block updates.

Reads use the stable declaration API independently of request time. Writes use
this override's own revision; parent settings and sibling revisions are
independent. Conflicts require a new plan. A committed write followed by a
failed read retains its known identity and revision. Before binding local
timestamp inputs, the follow-up read must return the exact committed child
revision. A concurrent edit reports a conflict and retains the committed
receipt.

Destroy retires the complete plan using `mode=all`, retaining its journal and
historical references. Cleanup is supported under inactive owners. Failures
retain state; confirmed absence of surviving coverage removes the resource from
state. Other overrides and parent settings are managed separately.

## Timestamps and timezone

`starts_at` and exclusive `ends_at` accept whole-second local
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` strings or explicit-offset RFC3339 instants. Zero-only
fractional digits are accepted. Input is sent unchanged. The API resolves local
values in the provider request `timezone`, stores UTC, returns offset timestamps
and rejects DST ambiguity or gaps. Explicit offsets identify absolute instants.

State preserves configured strings while private bindings to authoritative
server instants remain equivalent. Changed instants appear as drift. Import
adopts explicit-offset API values. Configured strings and private bindings
persist in Terraform state.

Changing an explicit provider `timezone` plans an update through computed
`request_timezone` for local inputs. Apply reinterprets the same strings in the
new zone; refresh preserves stored instants. Explicit-offset-only inputs do not
require a write for a request-zone change. Omitted provider timezone follows the
API actor's default without explicit zone tracking.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `schedule_overrides.create`,
`schedule_overrides.read`, `schedule_overrides.update` and
`schedule_overrides.delete`. Writes also require read authority for the
follow-up read. Parent schedules and memberships require their separate grants.
